chapters.title: Chapter 52 - The Great Demonic War (02)
paragraphs: "At that time, there was still no division between the orthodox and non-orthodox world, but when the war broke out, everything changed.
All the kingdoms and families had to take a side, support the powerful demon lord, or the declining orthodox sects, the Tang family was no different."
"And which did you choose?"
"Both," Yandu shook his head.
"The patriarch attached himself to the filthy hypocrites of the orthodox sects while the great elder left with young talents for the demon sect, forming the 13th demon clan.

The war lasted 15 grueling years, millions died and ended with a coalition of the leaders of the most powerful sects and families of the time storming the palace of the demon sect and beheading the demon lord."
Yandu paused for a moment, observing the curious expression on Qingyi’s face before continuing.
"But that wasn’t the end of it. The remaining clans gathered a large army and advanced against the orthodox sects, to take revenge and put an end to that war."
"And the demon cultivators lost," Qingyi commented, drawing a sigh from Yandu.
"Yes, but they weren’t the only losers."

"The great elder who had joined the demon lord used our forbidden technique. Filling the Nine Peaks Basin with poison and killing hundreds of millions, reducing the countless powerful sects that existed at the time to a mere handful."
Yandu’s voice shone, as if he were talking about the most incredible feat of all mankind, but he stopped at the last moment.
His eyes became opaque and a flicker of anger appeared on his face.
"That was the moment for our family to take control of this world, to forge a world under the power of poison, but do you know what they did?"
Yandu gritted his teeth, his voice turning into a growl.

"They begged for forgiveness! Our patriarch knelt to the heavens, vowed never again to use our power for any means other than noble and orthodox, destroying and scattering most of our secret techniques.
We’re a family of poisonous cultivators, born killers, but still, those damned old men cling to stupid ideals, refusing to face an enemy unless it’s head-on."
Yandu took a deep breath, controlling his anger.
"Don’t you think that’s pathetic?" he asked, turning his face to Qingyi.
"Clinging to these useless traditions, accepting being just one of the most powerful families on the Blue Moon Continent instead of embracing our true power and going to the horizon and beyond?"
Qingyi lowered his head, thinking for a brief moment.
It was an incredible story that he had never heard of.
Neither his master nor even the sect’s books had any information about this war beyond its name.
Knowing all this really broadened his horizon, but even so, there was something that made him uncomfortable.
Thinking about his words for a moment, Qingyi raised his head again. "Why are you telling me this?"
At those words, Tang Yandu smiled.
That was exactly the question he had been waiting for.
"Why don’t you come with me? Become my disciple. Together, we can rediscover our family’s lost techniques and shape this world in our own image!" Yandu exclaimed, looking at Qingyi expectantly.
"Just imbue a little of your Qi into my body, and I alone can free myself from my sister’s restrictions. I have a spatial technique to get us out of here in the blink of an eye."
Qingyi paused for a moment. That was a tempting proposition.
Despite his youthful appearance, Tang Yandu was an old master who had lived for over four hundred years and a great expert of the Nascent Soul Realm.
For someone with no future, following his plan would probably be the best course of action.
Unfortunately for him, Qingyi was not someone without a future.
The system was more than anything Tang Yandu could ever achieve.
"I’m sorry," Qingyi smiled. "As I said, I’m not as dumb as Young Master Xu."
Without even waiting for an answer, he turned his back on Yandu and walked out of the hut.
"Wait, we can think of something, I have a lot of hidden riches-" Tang Yandu’s voice was cut off by the slamming of the door.
"Ah..." He sighed. In his centuries of life, it was the first time he had met someone like this.
"Couldn’t my little sister have found a simpler man?" He gritted his teeth, but in the end just smiled bitterly.
That was impossible.

He had barely made contact with Tang Biyue, but he had already earned more lust points than he had in days of banging Feiyan.
He really wanted to spend it all and speed up his cultivation, but he held back, looking at the vast forest surrounding the mountain.
He had to find a way to escape from there, but he couldn’t act without thinking.
He was a long way from the sect’s territory and already close to the mountain range that surrounded the basin of the nine peaks.
The closer he got to it, the more powerful the beasts he could encounter.
In the golden sun city, he would rarely find anything other than Qi refining and foundation realm beasts, but here, there could even be burning blood realm beasts.
Simply running into the forest without planning would probably result in a very quick death.
"System... what do you recommend I do to get out of here?
[Item: Teleportation talisman
Description: A talisman that randomly teleports the user up to 100,000 kilometers.
It is slow to use and releases large amounts of energy.
Grade: Very Rare
"Ugh..." Qingyi felt his chest ache when he saw that price, but if it was truly necessary, what else could he do?
He was tempted to buy it right now, but when he saw the description, he gave up.
He could only use it if he was out of range of Tang Biyue’s senses, at least a few kilometers.
Otherwise, she would spot him immediately.
Sighing heavily, Qingyi got up, bought an apple from the system store and started eating it as he recovered to go back to training.
But he stopped after the first bite, raising his eyes towards the mountain ranges on the horizon.
The air shook and a horrible pressure fell on him.
An explosion of green mist rose into the sky and, even from a great distance, Qingyi could see it clearly.
Someone was fighting there, someone powerful.
Fortunately, the pressure didn’t last more than a few minutes, and he sighed heavily as he finally felt his chest calm down.
"Argh... what the fuck, did that come from Tang Biyue?" Qingyi gritted his teeth, standing up with difficulty.
Just... how powerful did that woman have to be to cause something like that?
"Ah..." Tang Biyue exhaled softly.
Her eyes were calm and her breathing soft and sweet.
Below her were the dead beasts, enough for their corpses to buy entire cities in the outer region of the Blue Moon Continent.
Her delicate feet touched the ground and a subtle smile played on her lips.
Although she wasn’t tired, her body was still covered in sweat.
The pale skin of her breasts exposed by a wide cleavage shone faintly in the sunlight, drops dripping from her chin and disappearing into the deep, soft valley of her twin mountains.
It had been many years since she had used her full power.
It was truly liberating.
Looking up, her beautiful green eyes closed, memories of the night before appearing in her mind.
That should never happen, not to someone of her level, and that made her anxious.
What was she supposed to do with Long Qingyi?
He was just an ant and killing him would be a wise choice, but she needed proof for that.
Every cultivator in the Tang family took an oath the moment they took their first step on the path of cultivation.
They were to fight for the good and never kill without justification.
Of course, these were just empty words and breaking them wouldn’t bring any real consequences, but she still resisted the idea.
She didn’t want to be like her brother.
"Ugh..." She sighed.
She really wanted to talk to her family elders and get an answer, but she erased that thought the next moment.
What was she supposed to tell them?
That one of the Tang family’s most powerful powerhouses was getting all wet because of a talentless ant who had barely stepped foot in the foundation realm?
The thought immediately made her lower her head.
A red flush spread across her soft, delicate cheeks.
Her full lips trembled slightly, but in the end, she just shook her head.
"One week," Biyue whispered.
She would train Qingyi for the next seven days.
If she didn’t find out anything, she would take him to her family elders.
They would probably find out something about what was going on.
With a smooth movement, her body floated gently before exploding into speed, quickly reaching where Qingyi was and landing softly in front of him.
Her eyes twitched slightly as she caught sight of the young man’s naked, sweaty torso.
Her gaze roamed over the defined, well-built muscles, every fiber of which seemed to have been carefully sculpted.
Not even high-level cultivators who had undergone several body reconstructions had such perfect bodies.
Why on earth was Qingyi like this?
The blush on her cheeks became even more intense before she took a deep breath and controlled herself.
"Get dressed and follow me," she said, her voice cold but pleasant.

chapters.title: Chapter 54 - too late for regrets
paragraphs: A week passed in the blink of an eye.
"Fuck!" Qingyi gritted his teeth as he swung his sword.
A loud bang echoed, followed by the agonizing roar of a beast as the lightning sword Qi tore through flesh and leather.
Qingyi stepped back momentarily, activating the lightning steps until his back hit a tree.
In front of him was a spiritual beast of the third stage of the Foundation Realm, an iron bull that stood more than three meters tall.
The creature’s powerful body was covered in terrible wounds, dark blood dripping down its metallic fur.
The iron bull bellowed furiously, raising its upper body while a powerful earth Qi accumulated in its hooves.
Sensing the danger, Qingyi activated his draconic eyes and the world seemed to slow down.
At the same time, the bull let its hooves fall to the soft earth.
The ground shook and an explosion spread through the forest, raising dust and throwing thousands of stone fragments everywhere.
Taking a deep breath, Qingyi jumped, slashing towards the dozens of projectiles coming towards him.
They were powerful and sharp, but they were nothing compared to Tianming’s last attack.
His lightning sword Qi easily cut through the stones, a blue aura covered in silver threads dancing around his body like luminous serpents.
When the dust finally settled, it revealed the beast sunk in a crater more than ten meters deep, its bloodshot eyes focused on Qingyi.
The young man wasted no time. He had to end it right there.
Calming his mind, he emptied his Dantian, pushing all his Qi towards his legs and his sword before advancing, feeling the metal shudder in his hands.
The bull realized the attack and roared, trying to protect itself with a metal wall, but it was too late.
The steel met its throat, the sword Qi cutting through the tough hide while the lightning Qi melted the flesh and meridians inside.
The beast stomped heavily on the ground, desperately trying to get away.
"You’re not going anywhere," Qingyi grunted as he lifted his right foot, dropping it on the bull’s legs.
A loud snap followed by a heartbreaking roar echoed as the beast’s heels broke off and its body collapsed on top of Qingyi.
Gritting his teeth, Qingyi forced the sword with everything he had, cutting through flesh, bone and muscle until it came out the other side of the neck.
The beast’s head fell with a deafening thud.
"Ugh..." Qingyi exhaled as he collapsed onto his knees, his body covered in blood and sweat.
Tang Biyue hadn’t given him a moment’s rest, forcing him to fight non-stop against foundation realm spiritual beasts, many of higher cultivation than his own.
If it hadn’t been for his draconic eyes and his lightning sword spirit root, he wouldn’t even have survived the first day.
With an exhausted sigh, he raised his head, watching the voluptuous beauty approaching.
Her beautiful green eyes were cold as she observed the beast’s corpse.
She seemed to hesitate for a brief moment before speaking: "I’ll take you to the family elders. We’ll leave tomorrow morning."
Without even giving Qingyi time to reply, she left, her voluptuous body disappearing among the trees.
"Shit..." Qingyi stood up, a touch of anger appearing on his face.
Why the hell was that woman so insistent?
Couldn’t she just mind her own business?
In the end, he could only shake his head in defeat.
He needed to get out of there as quickly as possible, but with her heightened senses, it would be almost impossible to do that...
As he reflected on his situation, he remembered something.
Her senses studied the mountain at almost all times, but she always seemed to withdraw them at night.
Qingyi himself was unable to perceive her senses, but Tang Yandu, even with his cultivation blocked, could still sense them.
It was only at the moments when her senses were retracted that Yandu tried to get Qingyi to release him.
"Just wait..." A smile played on Qingyi’s lips as she walked towards the hut.
The moment Tang Yandu started making his countless promises of power and wealth, he would run away.
When he entered the hut, he found Tang Yandu with his eyes closed, meditating peacefully.
Ignoring him, Qingyi sat down on the other side of the room and also closed his eyes, only opening them when Tang Yandu’s voice woke him up.
"What do you think’s going to happen, huh?"
Hearing these words, Qingyi slowly opened his eyes.
"My sister," Yandu smiled mischievously.
"She’s interested in you, in something inside you, and not for something good. She wouldn’t have kept you here for so long if it was good."
When Qingyi stood up, Yandu hurried his voice.
"They’re going to open you up, kid! The elders will look inside your guts and even if they find nothing and decide to keep you alive, you’ll never be able to cultivate again!"
Qingyi opened the door, ignoring Yandu’s desperate words.
"Hey, where do you think you’re going? Do you think you can escape from my sister on your own? Unless you have a teleportation talisman, it’s impossible!
But I can help you, just imbue some of your Qi into my meridians and-."
Yandu’s words were silenced when the door closed with a bang.
"Fuck..." He gritted his teeth, banging the back of his head against the wall as he thought about how to get out of the situation.
Even in the best case scenario, he would probably be crippled and forced to live as a monk.
Death would even be a mercy compared to what would happen if the great sects intervened in his trial.
He would probably have his mind completely scanned for information about the rebirth of the demonic cult, a process that often resulted in the destruction of the soul.
Just thinking about it was enough to make him shudder with terror.
If he could go back in time, he would probably do everything differently.
Unfortunately, it was too late for regrets.
Without Qingyi’s help, it was impossible for him to escape his sister and his father’s judgment.

chapters.title: Chapter 55 - Escape
paragraphs: Long Qingyi jumped over the treetops, landing silently on a branch.
His eyes scanned everything around him. It was dark, but with his draconic eyes activated, he could see clearly.
During the seven days he had been trained by Tang Biyue, he had not only greatly increased his control over Qi and his battle capabilities, but he had also studied various escape routes.
That place was known as the Beast Land.
It was a territory controlled entirely by spirit creatures and one of the main barriers separating the outer area of the Blue Moon Continent from the Nine Peaks Basin.
The mountain they stood on was in a deep valley, surrounded by dense forests, imposing mountains and winding canyons.
To the north and east, he would encounter beasts whose power reached the Iron Body Realm, while to the west, in the mountain ranges, there were even beasts of the Burning Blood Realm.
Going to any of those regions would be suicide, any beast above the Iron Body Realm would be able to kill him before he even felt its presence.
"Only the south remains..." he whispered to himself.
The south was the region with the fewest and weakest beasts.
The most powerful were only in the Golden Core Realm, with the majority in the Foundation Realm.
Of course, it was still dangerous, but Tang Yandu’s words made him ignore this danger completely.
He couldn’t be taken into the Tang family; if he allowed that to happen, it would be the end for him.
"System... how far away do I have to be to activate the talisman without being caught by Tang Biyue?"
[At least twenty kilometers. The talisman’s activation time is thirty seconds].
"Hm... that’ll have to do." He sighed, opening the system store and buying the talisman.
He couldn’t help but feel his heart ache as a golden piece of paper appeared in his hands and more than ten thousand lust points disappeared from his status.
He looked at the golden paper, which glowed faintly. He could feel a powerful Qi emanating from the words on it.
Putting the talisman away, he turned south.
"Twenty kilometers..." he repeated to himself, activating the Lightning Steps.
As a Foundation Realm cultivator, he could run at more than 60 kilometers per hour, even without using his movement techniques.
If he used his movement skills, it wouldn’t take him more than a few minutes to reach a safe distance.
His body disappeared into the darkness of the night and, slowly, the mountain began to move away.
The further he got, the more presences he felt - pulses of spiritual energy and horrendous roars echoing through the forest.
That was a dangerous forest to venture into at night.
Tang Biyue’s presence kept any beast away, but the moment he passed the fifteen-kilometer mark, that protection ended.
Qingyi immediately felt several auras falling on him.
His body trembled and his legs almost failed him, but he resisted, enveloping himself in a mantle of silver-blue Qi as he cut through the dense forest.
When he finally reached the twenty-kilometer mark, he stopped. His eyes shone as he raised his sword.
A crash echoed, his arms almost giving way as he was catapulted towards the ground, his body opening a small crater on impact.
"Crystal Serpent! Peak Foundation Realm!" Qingyi’s eyes widened as he hastily stood up.
In front of him, a monstrous figure stretched more than twenty meters in length.
Its eyes were a deep black and its white, almost translucent scales reflected the moonlight.
Without wasting any time, Qingyi grabbed the teleportation talisman, tearing it in half.
[Teleportation talisman activating in 30 seconds...]
Qingyi read the system notification, but barely paid any attention to it.
His eyes were fixed on the beast as the pieces of the talisman rose into the sky, glowing with an intense golden light.
The serpent hissed with that light.
Its forked tongue felt the air for a brief moment before it opened a mouth full of thin, sharp teeth and advanced towards Qingyi.
Its colossal body tore up the ground as it moved, snaking through the closed forest.
Strands of Qi that seemed to be made of crystals spread out above it, burning everything they touched.
Qingyi dodged and escaped the creature’s jaws, but its tail still hit him.
A deafening bang echoed, Qingyi coughing up blood as he was thrown backwards once again.
[15 seconds]
He showed a bloody smile on his face, activating Lightning Steps and swinging his sword towards the spirit beast, which tried to swallow him again.
Qingyi narrowly dodged it, jumping over its head and parrying its tail with his glowing blade.
He pushed every ounce of Lightning Sword Qi out of his Dantian, roared, and forced his arms until they went limp, but achieved nothing but a small mark on the creature’s scales.
[5 seconds]
The snake swung its colossal body and a muffled grunt escaped Qingyi’s lips as he hit a tree.
Some of his ribs broke and one of his lungs filled with blood.
[3 seconds]
The snake retracted its head, muscles rippling under its crystalline scales.
[2 seconds]
It opened its huge mouth, revealing rows of dagger-sharp fangs.
[1 second]
It advanced towards Qingyi, its jaw closing around him.
[Teleportation talisman activated]
Tang Biyue suddenly woke up.
Someone of her level could go for weeks without sleeping, but she still liked to do it from time to time.
It helped her think better.
Her beautiful green eyes fluttered slightly as she left her residence.
Her senses immediately picked up a strong source of energy.
With a smooth leap, she shot off in that direction, landing on a newly formed crater.
Her eyes were cold as they surveyed the battlefield.
With a single movement of her delicate hands, a colossal, bloody head fell, the body of the Crystal Serpent convulsing.
"He’s gone..." she said, her voice almost a whisper as she raised her head, looking at the beautiful moonlight that illuminated her serene face and the pale, voluptuous skin of her breasts.
Honestly, that was the best for her.
She was destined to live for thousands of years after reaching the Transcendence Realm, while Qingyi probably wouldn’t last more than a few centuries.
It was only natural.
She would never see him again and wouldn’t have to deal with the problem with her family’s elders.
But even so, she couldn’t help feeling a strange heaviness in her heart.
"Ah..." she let out a soft sigh.
It was time to take her brother to trial.
She couldn’t waste any more time.

chapters.title: Chapter 56 - Milf paradise (01)
paragraphs: The Heavenly Thunder Kingdom was a small, forgotten country in the westernmost regions of the Blue Moon Continent, located on an island a few dozen kilometers off the coast of the continent.
Being in a remote region, the Qi here was even less dense than in the rest of the outer region of the Blue Moon Continent.
Here, even foundation realm cultivators were rare, with only a handful of golden core cultivators existing in the entire realm.
And in this realm, hidden in a deep valley, was a small, well-kept temple.
"Sister Yueli!" A sweet, youthful voice called out to a woman who was kneeling by a stream, peacefully washing clothes.
The owner of that voice was a slender young woman with black hair and big eyes.
"What happened? Why the rush?" Qin Yueli asked as she stood up.
She was a stunning woman, her dark blue hair was tied up elegantly, framing a beautiful, mature face.
Her elegant white robes were slightly damp, the thin, wet fabric clinging to her skin, its translucence revealing her peaky, pink nipples.
"The red claw gang! They’re back and they’re saying they’ll burn down the temple if we don’t open the gates!" The young woman spoke hurriedly.
Yueli’s beautiful blue eyes twitched and she quickly grabbed a sword from beside her dirty clothes.
Although it didn’t look like it, she was a swordswoman who had trained all her life.
Her cultivation was only at the first stage of the foundation realm, but her power was not something to be ignored in the Heavenly Thunder Kingdom.
Her body was taken over by a thunderous mantle and she bit her red lips, advancing towards the temple.
"Open that damn gate and wait for us with your legs open! So I, Hei Lang, promise to consider not cutting off your heads after I’ve finished with you!" A bald man with a powerful body roared.
When his voice ceased, sadistic, lust-filled laughter echoed among his men, more than a hundred of them.
They all wore red jackets and their faces bore horrible scars and rotting teeth.
Their lustful gazes swept over the temple walls and the women who watched them with disgust.
There were eighteen of them and each one was a great beauty, untouched by the world.
Just imagining them naked was enough to make the bandits’ mouths drool with anticipation.
Hei Lang drew his great saber, the silver blade extending almost a meter and a half.
If they didn’t open the gate, he would bring it down.
A sadistic smile played on his dry lips as he advanced towards the temple.
"Get lost!" A feminine roar cut through the air, and he raised his saber instinctively.
His feet sank into the ground as he was forced back more than ten meters. In front of the gate, stood a mature, voluptuous beauty.
Hei Lang’s eyes flashed, sweeping over Yueli’s generous hips and delicate waist before settling on the pale, soft skin of her breasts, threatening to escape from her wet robe.
"Oh, my dear Yueli... have you finally come to give yourself to me?" Hei Lang laughed, licking a scar on his lower lip.
They were both Foundation Realm cultivators and had crossed swords a few times.
Qin Yueli gritted her teeth, her beautiful face distorting into a scowl as she looked at the men behind Hei Lang.

chapters.title: Chapter 65 - "Have more faith in me"
paragraphs: "I’m sorry about the girls, young master Qingyi... they’re a bit... eccentric," Qin Yueli apologized as she sat next to Qingyi, watching the priestesses train.
Strangely, they seemed even more excited now that Qingyi was staying with them.
"They were taken in by master when they were still very young. Elize and I failed to teach them common sense..." Yueli’s eyes swept over Qingyi’s body.
"It’s okay, they’re cute," Qingyi replied with a low laugh.
And it wasn’t as if Yueli or Elize were great sources of common sense either, far from it.
The handsome young man kept a gentle smile on his lips, his clothes disheveled by hugs and tugs, even marked with lipstick.
That wasn’t exactly common treatment in a closed and conservative society, but who was he to judge them?
He was blessed with transcendental beauty and possessed a system that made him even more irresistible, especially to lower-level cultivators who were more susceptible to the lust system.
"Cute?" Yueli’s lips twitched as she hugged her own legs, her head resting lazily on her arms.
Her beautiful blue eyes studied Qingyi with interest.
"Ah... I mean, they’re... well..." Qingyi was speechless.
How on earth could he explain himself?
"Hahaha, that’s okay, it’s true, they’re cute..." Yueli laughed, her sweet, soft voice echoing through the temple and briefly catching the girls’ attention.
But her expression soon turned serious and her laughter died down.
"Master always told me to keep you away from the horrors of this world, that one day a hero would come to take the spirit of lightning and lead our temple to the top of the world again."
"I wonder where this hero is..."
Hearing those words, Qingyi’s face also lost its smile.
A lightning spirit linked to a powerful sword that was once an artifact of the heavenly sky.
Honestly, that was perfect for him.
There were three main types of weapon.
The first were ordinary weapons, made of metals of different strengths and resistances.
Then came spirit swords, such as the Thunderclouds sword.
These were weapons made of spiritual materials that carried unique elements and could increase the power of a specific type of Qi by a wide margin.
And then there was the third type.
These were also spirit swords, but with one simple difference: they had their own egos.
Unlike ordinary and spiritual swords, a cultivator needed to dominate a sword with an ego and be accepted by it.
Failure would often result in death.
’System... what is the cheapest spiritual sword with an ego that I could buy?’ Qingyi asked mentally, his heart sinking at the sight of the prices.
It was simply absurd.
An common grade sword cost thousands of lust points.
"Miss Yueli... where is this sword?" He asked, feeling the handle of the borrowed sword in his hands.
It was a good blade, and he could easily buy one suitable for his level with the amount of lust points he had.
But wanting more isn’t a sin, is it?
"Are you thinking of trying to be accepted by it?"
"Yes," he nodded.
The blue-haired beauty shuddered at his answer.
"Qingyi..." His lips opened, a soft tremor running through his voice. "My master was killed trying to be accepted, and not just her. Every year, thousands die trying to be accepted by that sword."
She paused for a brief moment and her eyes focused on the ground, avoiding Qingyi’s intense gaze.
Why did he always have to look at her like that? Her cheeks were overcome by a faint blush.
"You’ve been very good to me and my sisters. They seem to really like having you here, I don’t want you to die like that... the way the master died..."
"Ah..." Qingyi exhaled, drawing his sword as he stood up, the silver steel sliding into the scabbard with a sharp hiss.
"What are you doing?"
"Why don’t we train a bit more? I’ve just had a breakthrough and I wanted to test out some of my new power," Qingyi interrupted her.
"A breakthrough?" Yueli stood up in surprise.
Qingyi didn’t seem to be close to a breakthrough.
Only now did she realize that no matter how much she focused her senses; she couldn’t sense his cultivation.
She hesitated for a brief moment, but in the end just shook her head, following him to the middle of the courtyard.
She felt a slight discomfort in her chest at Qingyi’s lack of response about trying to be accepted by the lightning spirit.
But she quickly pushed it aside. Thinking too much wouldn’t solve the problem.
Yueli moved her delicate hands, grasping the scabbard before sliding her silvery blade out.
Her gaze swept over her sisters, who quickly stopped their training, surrounding them with curiosity.
"Let’s get out of the courtyard, it’s dangerous," Elize grabbed the girls’ shoulders, gently pulling them away, her beautiful purple eyes studying Qingyi with concern.
She had heard their conversation at a glance and couldn’t help but feel her chest tremble.
Her master was at the Golden Core realm and still ended up dead.
How could Qingyi stand a chance?
With the entire central courtyard cleared for them, Yueli finally released her aura.
Thunderous lightning streaked across her silver blade, her beautiful blue eyes shining brightly.
"Are you really fully recovered?" she asked.
She had seen Qingyi kill dozens of men in a minute, chopping off the hands of a fourth-stage Foundation Realm cultivator as if he were a simple farmer.
She knew well that there was no point in holding back if he had already fully recovered.
"Yes," Qingyi nodded, releasing his own Foundation Realm aura. "I’ll give you the first move," he smiled, not thinking it would take more than that.
Yueli thanked him, her eyes becoming sharp as the ground beneath her feet shook.
In a split second, she cut the distance between them, her sword tearing through the air and scattering sparks of lightning.
Qingyi only raised his sword slightly, parrying Yueli’s.
A bang echoed, and their surroundings shook.
High-pitched screams reached his ears as the girls’ dresses were swept away by the shockwave of the collision.
And then, a sword flew out.
"H-how?" Yueli shuddered, looking down at her delicate, trembling hands.
She could feel that Qingyi had barely used a fraction of his Qi, yet it was as if he had hit an impassable barrier...
Her eyes rose slightly, meeting his.
"Have more faith in me," he smiled, moving his right hand and stroking her head.
"Uh?" Yueli froze, vibrant red spreading across her cheeks.
"Oh..." Qingyi quickly withdrew his hand.
He forgot that Yueli was a thirty five year old woman.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 -Tempest Monarch Sword Art
paragraphs: Alone in his room, Qingyi sighed tiredly as he sat on his bed.
He had fucked Elize until the moon appeared in the sky, and then continued fucking her until their naked bodies collapsed on top of each other.
Now, at dawn, he wanted to have her in his arms, his face sinking into those huge breasts.
Unfortunately, he had to hold back.
The other women still didn’t know that he had taken Elize and, honestly, he preferred to proceed more slowly.
He could easily take them right now, as he had done with Elize. The difference in cultivation was too great for them to resist his lineage.
But in the end, he just shook his head. He didn’t want to force anything, at least not yet.
Pushing those lustful thoughts from his mind, he focused on his status screen.
[Name: Long Qingyi
Age: 18
Cultivation: Second stage of the foundation realm (700 lust points to upgrade)
Affinities: Lightning 60 - Sword: 60 - Charm: 1000 (can be upgraded in the lust store)
Spiritual roots: Seventh level lightning sword root (1000 lust points to upgrade, new roots can be bought in the lust store). )
Lineage: Blood of the Corruption Dragon God (Rare grade, 10,000 lust points to upgrade.)
Constitution: Body of the primordial dragon (Rare grade, 10,000 lust points to upgrade.)
Lust points: 3137]
His fun with Elize had earned him just over a thousand lust points, enough to make him comfortable.
He could continue improving his spiritual root, but he rejected the idea immediately.
His root was already not much inferior to a ninth level one and, with the density of Qi in this region, he would hardly gain much from a new spirit root.
So there were three things he could improve.
The first was obviously a good sword that could withstand all his foundation realm power.
Right after that, a new movement or combat technique.
The first option was something Qingyi was resisting doing, he was still interested in the spirit of lightning and the sword it inhabited.
It wasn’t worth spending a fortune on a good sword only to replace it when he managed to conquer a spirit sword with an ego, far more powerful than anything he could buy now.
Movement techniques were also something he didn’t want to change just yet.
Lightning steps could easily last him until he reached the golden core realm, perhaps even beyond that.
It was a very reliable technique, even though it was only a rare grade.
And then there were the combat techniques.
These were probably what Qingyi needed most at the moment.
Since he did not had any other combat techniques, this would immediately increase his fighting capacity by a long margin, while at the same time bringing no risk of redundancy.

Of course, there were still other things like artifacts, spiritual robes and attack and defense talismans, but none of them would represent as big a leap in Qingyi’s power as a proper combat technique.
Making his decision, Qingyi opened the system store, looking at the almost infinite list of techniques.
"Ah..." he exhaled.
The amount of techniques was staggering, at a level where even filtering, there were still tens of thousands.
’Where does all this stuff come from?’ he thought, his eyes skimming through the descriptions of dozens of techniques.
After long minutes of searching, something finally caught his eye.
[Combat technique: Tempest Monarch Sword Art Fragment
Grade: Rare

Description: An ancient sword technique that uses lightning Qi, created by a dynasty of lightning cultivators from the ancient era, is divided into twelve forms. This fragment contains the first and second forms.
Price: 2500 lust points]
"Hm..." Qingyi scratched his chin.
Honestly, it was hard to tell how good those techniques were from the descriptions alone.
But one thing caught his eye about the Tempest Monarch’s sword art.
Although it was only a fragment, it was a technique from the ancient era, also known as the golden age of martial arts on the Blue Moon Continent, more than a hundred thousand years ago.
"System, filter only for rare grade techniques from the ancient era," Qingyi ordered and, in the next moment, the list of tens of thousands of techniques was reduced to just a hundred.
The Storm Monarch Sword Art Fragment was the cheapest of these hundred, with the most expensive ones costing tens of thousands of lust points.
But Qingyi was well aware that this price was not excessive.
Ancestral techniques were on a completely different level; a mortal-grade technique could give you an empire, but a mortal-grade ancestral technique could give you the heavens.
Removing any doubt from his heart, Qingyi moved his fingers, pressing buy on the technique.
2,500 lust points disappeared from his status and, in the next moment, he felt a sharp pain, an almost endless stream of information flooding into his head.
It was similar to what he felt with the lightning steps, but much more intense, as if the lightning steps were a short poem and the Tempest Monarch Sword Art Fragment was an endless epic.
It was only after almost five minutes of suffering that Qingyi stood up, sighing with relief.
Without wasting any time, he immediately left his room, leaping over the temple walls and taking up a distance where he wouldn’t wake the girls.
His long black hair danced lightly in the cool early morning breeze as he looked up, the moonlight bathing his handsome face.
With a smooth movement, he drew his sword, the steel cutting through the air before being taken over by a thunderous aura.
But this was no ordinary aura, it was much more intense.
The air around him seemed to boil as Qingyi used the first form of the Tempest Monarch sword art.
A boom echoed as he struck, lightning leaving the tip of the sword and sweeping over everything more than ten meters in front of Qingyi.
The ground shook as the trees in front of him fell to the forest floor.
Their trunks were burning, but not in flames - they were melting.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 -The tanned beauty
paragraphs: The capital of the Golden Sun Kingdom was one of the largest cities on the Blue Moon Continent, with almost five million inhabitants and teeming with life even at night.
Its streets were well lit. The brothels, taverns and even teahouses were still overflowing with customers, even though it was late at night.
Away from the busy main streets, two figures walked in the darkness.
Both were covered in cloaks of spiritual silk, only their faces barely visible in the dim light that met them.
The first had an aged face and a gentle smile.
The second possessed incomparable beauty, her mature, tanned features dotted with subtle, elegant make-up, blood-red lips and beautiful, piercing brown eyes.
But those beautiful eyes were shaky, as were her steps.
"Master..." Hua Feiyan’s lips opened slightly, drawing Madame Xue’s attention.
"What is it, dear?" Madame Xue stopped her steps, her aged eyes scanning her dear disciple’s worried expression.
"Are you sure about this woman?" Feiyan asked, her fingers anxiously intertwined.
"Ah..." Madame Xue exhaled heavily before looking up at the sky, the stars dimmed by light pollution.
"I once had a husband... I was terribly in love with him, to the point where my heart would break just by spending a night away from each other..."
"During the war between the three great sects and the Kingdom of the Golden Sun a hundred and fifty years ago, he disappeared.
For more than twenty years, I searched for him..." Madame Xue’s words died away briefly.
There was pain in them, a pain long suppressed but still there.
"It was this woman who helped me find his body and give him a proper burial."
Hearing those words, Feiyan shuddered, lowering her face.
What if she found out that her Qingyi was actually dead?
What if all she got was a place where she would find a sun-dried corpse?
It made her breathing uneasy and her heart bleed.
But she controlled herself, calmed her mind and took a step forward.
She had already cried everything she had to cry, nights without being able to sleep and days without being able to eat.
She was tired of it.
She knew that her Qingyi wouldn’t like to see her like this.
"Let’s go." Madame Xue smiled and they soon arrived at a small, shabby house.
"You must enter alone. A drop of blood is all the payment she needs."
Hua Feiyan nodded silently before entering the house.
Her steps were a little uncertain.
Why would someone with such peculiar power hide in such an inappropriate place?
But the moment she stepped through the door, she realized that this was no ordinary place.
Her mind was taken over by a calming aura, her eyes lost their worry and her steps stopped shaking.
"Have you lost your beloved, my dear?" A voice called out to her, old and hoarse, carrying a maternal gentleness.
Feiyan immediately felt her heart tremble, her eyes focusing on an old woman sitting casually, her hands resting on an orb on a table.
How did she know that?
"Sit down, honey. I believe you’re in a hurry, aren’t you?"
Feiyan paused for a single moment, but in the end bit her lower lip before stepping forward and sitting down in a chair opposite the old woman.
Without hesitation, she brought her index finger to her teeth, tearing the delicate skin before raising it over the orb. A single drop of blood dripped from the wound.
A bright smile came over the old woman, who grabbed Feiyan’s hands, placing them under the orb and closing her eyes.
"Tell me, darling... who was this man to you?"
"He was my everything."
"And how far would you go for him?"
"Until my soul is gone."
"Hm..." The old woman looked surprised. Both answers were the absolute truth.
That kind of customer was rare. Most always had a small lie among their statements.
"And how far do you think he would go for you?" she asked.
"I know that not even the heavens would stop him.
"You know? And what gives you that confidence?"
"Because he’s my Qingyi." Feiyan replied, and the old woman’s smile intensified.
Another truth.
"Close your eyes, dear. I can feel your beloved." The old woman instructed and Feiyan obeyed without question.
The next moment, she felt a strange energy enter her hands.
It wasn’t like the Qi she was used to. It was thin, subtle, almost as if it had no real presence.
And then she felt her obscured vision light up. For a brief moment, she saw it.
Standing among a trail of destruction, a handsome young man with long black hair and piercing eyes.
His sword was drawn, but there was no enemy around. He was just casually practicing.
It all lasted only a single second before Feiyan’s vision was drawn back to her body.
Her heart almost burst out of her chest and tears ran down her cheeks.
Her Qingyi was alive, his body without a single injury, to the point where he could even train in a relaxed manner.
She had never felt so relieved in her entire life, as if she had been carrying a cargo ship on her chest and that ship had suddenly become a small toy boat.
"Thank you very much-" Feiyan suddenly stood up, ready to say thank you, but as the words left her lips, she realized that she was already outside.
The house had disappeared, replaced by an ordinary commercial establishment.
Her watery eyes scanned everything around her, soon meeting those of her master.
"Good news?" Madame Xue laughed, realizing that the tears in her disciple’s eyes were not tears of sorrow.
They were tears of happiness.
"Thank you, master! I promise to train hard and reach the golden core realm before the alchemy tournament!" Feiyan threw herself into Madame Xue’s arms, hugging her tightly.
Her Qingyi was alive and well.
She was sure of that now. Even if they couldn’t meet right now, she was still happy.
She knew he would be back soon.

chapters.title: Chapter 71 - Are you sure?
paragraphs: "Ah..." The old woman sighed heavily as Hua Feiyan disappeared from her office.
Alone, an evil smile played across her face, her eyes focusing on Feiyan’s blood.
There was something powerful about it, the kind she had never experienced in centuries of cultivating divination arts.
She moved her aged fingers across her orb, the crimson liquid sticking to her pale skin.
Hesitating for a brief moment, she popped it into her mouth and her body shuddered.
Her face was overcome by a deep ecstasy as her body arched. How could such a taste exist?
Not even the most powerful experts who had ever offered their blood to her had such intense flavors.
It was powerful and pure, too pure for any mortal woman to possess.
"I..." The old woman’s lips slowly opened.
She wanted more, her eyes were filled with murderous intent and greed, but she held back.
From the depths of that blood, she felt something else, even purer than Feiyan’s blood.
Strangely, her body seemed incapable of breaking down and absorbing it, even with her cultivation of the Iron Body realm.
It was simply impossible.
"This... has something to do with that brat?" Her eyes twitched, remembering the figure she had shown Feiyan.
That was a common divination technique, which used strong feelings to briefly pick up on someone’s presence in the world.
High-level experts could easily foil these techniques, but cultivators like Qingyi, without any kind of protection, were a perfect target for divination masters.
"I wonder..." A sickening smile appeared on his wrinkled face, and a powerful golden Qi took over his crystal orb. "What will his fate be?"
Seeing someone’s fate was a dangerous technique for most divination masters; they only used it when very necessary.
But she ignored these risks.
Wealthy clients asked to see fate all the time. Once, she even saw the fate of a young boy who was destined to be a Rebirth Realm expert.
Yet all she suffered was a nosebleed.
What were the chances of that young man having a fate that came even close to that?
Calming her breathing, she focused on Feiyan’s blood.
"As I imagined..." she smiled, sensing two interlocking barriers. One of them was Feiyan’s fate, the other Qingyi’s.
Without hesitation, she forced her Qi onto the barrier.
As it was based on the target’s cultivation level, it wasn’t difficult to break through.
And then she saw Qingyi’s fate.
A star, purple, shining, above everything and everyone, beyond anything her mind could comprehend.
The pressure of the star immediately fell on the image she had formed of Qingyi’s fate.
Her eyes widened and she immediately tried to back away, but it was too late.
Her meridians shuddered as all the Qi she hadn’t used to break the barrier collapsed.
Her eyes were filled with an explosion of blood and her skin turned red.
She tried to struggle, to calm her energy, but nothing helped.
After a few more moments of suffering, her body collapsed onto the ground, her aura slowly disappearing.
"Uh?" Qingyi looked up, feeling a slight strangeness in his chest.
"Ah..." He sighed before shaking his head and circulating his Qi, calming his mind.
He had trained throughout the night, slowly perfecting the first two forms of the Tempest Monarch Sword Art.
He was still far from mastering them, but at least he had enough control for them to be useful in combat.
Qingyi stood up, hearing a soft knock on the door.
When he opened it, his vision immediately met a mature beauty with purple hair and gentle eyes.
Realizing that no one was looking, he grabbed her slender, delicate wrists, pulling her into an embrace.
"Nghn~~ Not now..." Elize pushed against his chest, but couldn’t resist.
"And why not?" He asked, his hands moving up from her delicate waist to her huge, soft twin mountains, feeling them give way under his fingers.
"S-sister Yueli... she’s waiting for you in the throne room..."
Hearing these words, Qingyi controlled himself, his hands returning to her waist before sinking his lips to hers.
"You’re even hotter today, you know that?" A subtle smile took over Qingyi’s face as their lips parted.
Elize didn’t reply, just sinking her face into Qingyi’s chest, accepting his embrace, her body warm against his.
"Sister Yueli is in a hurry, she still needs to go buy supplies in the village..." She murmured softly.
Elize just wanted to melt into Qingyi’s arms and stay there for the rest of eternity, but she knew she couldn’t, at least not yet.
After a few more moments of caressing, Qingyi finally sighed heavily before letting go of the purple-haired beauty.
His eyes held a bit of sorrow as he left his room and looked towards the large pavilion in the center of the temple.
He hadn’t yet entered the temple’s throne room and was quite curious. That place was different from all the rest of the temple; its construction wasn’t rustic and archaic.
On the contrary, its pillars were made of white marble surrounded by gold threads and its large double doors were a deep purple.
He raised his hand to knock on the doors, but it wasn’t necessary.
With a creak, they opened, revealing a luxurious interior, large enough to fit more than a hundred people.
The floor was covered in a carpet as soft as the most comfortable bed Qingyi had ever slept in, second only to Feiyan and Elize’s bosoms.
And then, far in the background, he could see Yueli’s delicate back, her beautiful blue eyes focused on a large throne that was more like the armchairs of Earth, covered in a cushion as soft as silk.
"Is everything all right?" Qingyi asked, a little uncertain.
"Yes..." Yueli lowered her head before standing up, her eyes meeting Qingyi’s.
"Your night seems to have been fruitful, congratulations on your breakthrough." Qingyi smiled, noticing that Yueli’s aura was much deeper.
She had advanced to the second stage of the foundation realm.
"Thank you, you also seem to have had some level of comprehension." Yueli returned his smile, but her expression soon turned serious.
"Young master Qingyi..." She spoke, hesitating for a single moment before continuing. "Are you sure you want to go after the lightning spirit?"

The qi was even thinner than in the temple, to the point that just standing there was enough to make a cultivator uncomfortable.
"Oh... Lady Qin!" An old woman sitting in front of the village gate stood up, her eyes widening at the sight of Qingyi just behind Yueli.
Everyone in the village knew Qin Yueli.
She visited the place once every few months, bought tons of supplies and then disappeared.
But she had always been alone.
Everyone knew about the temple, an isolated place where only women entered, but even those women never accompanied Yueli there.
Yet there she was, accompanied by a handsome man who gripped her hips as if she were everything to him.
Yueli ignored all the strange looks, continuing on with Qingyi until they finally reached the only shop in the village.
"Oh... esteemed cultivator, what can I do for you?" The store owner, a sly-looking old man with gray hair, bowed slightly as he clasped his hands together.
While Yueli shopped, Qingyi walked around the store.
It was a poor place, the products were mostly grains and some low-quality drinks.
As he walked past the shelves, something finally caught his eye.
It was a bottle of wine which, even closed, exuded a strong, alcoholic smell.
Taking it in his hands, Qingyi studied it.
It was clearly a high-quality wine, unlike the cheap liquors that the old man sold in gourds.
"I see you have good eyes, young cultivator! This is royal wine, I got it more than ten years ago when a prince visited our village! It’s been waiting for an owner ever since, hehehe."
The old man laughed, his eyes filling with greed as he looked at Qingyi’s clothes.
They were clean, made of a soft, pure silk. Qingyi must have had a lot of money!
"How much?" the handsome young man asked, studying the bottle for a few more moments.
"Just 15 gold coins, hehehe!"
Hearing that price, Qingyi shuddered.
15 gold coins? That damned old man was trying to rob him in broad daylight!
He could buy spirit wine, of a quality hundreds of times better, for 12 gold coins in the City of Golden Clouds!
"Oh... has the price gone down?" Yueli’s eyes lit up at the old man’s words.
"Do you want me to buy it for you? There’ll still be a bit left over after I’ve bought the supplies for the girls.
"No need..." Qingyi shook his head, a little awkwardly.
He had forgotten that he was no longer in the Ascending Dragon Sect.
Now, he was in an even more isolated place, where the ordinary wines he could find in the sect would be priceless treasures.
Sighing, he bought a few gold coins from the system, handing them to the old man before taking the wine.
As he walked back to Yueli’s side, he observed the supplies being placed on the floor by the store staff.
Tons, not just of grains and fruit, but mainly of liquors.
"Do you really need that much?" he asked, looking at the barrels and barrels of liquor piling up.
"Honestly, it’s a bit lacking..." Yueli smiled awkwardly.
The priestesses at the temple drank a lot, and she couldn’t deny that she was partly to blame for that.

When the employees had finished putting everything away, Yueli took out a small bag from her robes, opening it and shaking it gently before a huge suction power came out of its entrance, pulling all the supplies inside.
"All set?" Qingyi asked, little surprised.
That was a space bag, very similar to space rings, only of a much lower price and quality.
"Yes..." Yueli ducked her head as they left the store and headed out of the village.
She didn’t like the place or the people there very much.
They weren’t honest and the men always looked at her disgustingly.
Sighing heavily, her beautiful eyes focused on Qingyi as she grabbed Bluey’s reins.
Her lips opened slightly, but stopped the next second.
Qingyi’s face distorted and a powerful aura took over his body as he advanced towards the forest like a blur.
"Fuck!" A painful grunt echoed as Qingyi’s hands closed around a man’s neck.
He was bald, deep-set and wearing a red jacket.
"The Red Claw gang!" Yueli recognized him immediately.

sentences.text: Bluey trotted lightly along a short but well-tended trail.
Yueli, still panting and flushed, allowed herself to sink into Qingyi’s arms, her head resting against his chest.
Her body felt strange, but not in a bad way.
A subtle warmth seized her chest while her lips were unable to hide their shy smile.
Qingyi’s hands circled her slender waist, flowing down to her lean, delicate belly before moving up to her breasts.
He grasped the twin peaks with both hands, feeling the soft, creamy skin as his fingers sank into the soft flesh.
"Mmm..." She sighed softly and closed her eyes.
It was comfortable.
She wouldn’t mind staying there for the rest of her life.
"What would you do?
If you really managed to conquer the lightning spirit?" she asked, breaking the silence between them.

"Upper heavens?
You mean the immortal heaven?" Yueli’s eyes twitched.
"Yes, and what’s above it." The handsome young man smiled.
"What, do you think your husband is too ambitious?"
"Hm... no, I like ambition..." Yueli returned his smile, but her face soon turned serious.
"The master has always dreamed of ascending, of going beyond the mortal sky and spreading the cult of the spirit of lightning throughout the world..." Her voice lost a little of its strength.
"Ah..." Qingyi exhaled heavily as he hugged her even tighter.
"You have no resentment?
Of the lightning spirit, of what it did to your master and to... well, all the others who tried to conquer it."
"Sometimes..." Yueli snuggled a little closer, her beautiful blue eyes misty.
"But I know there’s a reason behind it, that she would never hurt us if she had a choice..."
"I understand..." Qingyi shook his head and didn’t go any further.
It was something painful for her, he didn’t need much to realize it.

chapters.title: Chapter 75 - The Invasion
paragraphs: The bandit from the Red Claw gang tried to fight against Qingyi’s grip, but the moment he felt the young man’s power, he gave up.
Filling his gaze with determination, he opened his mouth, biting a small capsule between his teeth.
The substance spread through his body, his skin turned purple and a disgusting black blood leaked from his mouth.
"Ugh!" Qingyi quickly withdrew his hand, watching the corpse melt as it fell to the ground.
That was truly cruel poison, not even leaving bones behind.
Turning his face, his eyes met those of Yueli. She was trembling.
If there was already an escort from the Red Claw gang there, didn’t that mean that the main force was already getting close to the temple?
The mere thought of this possibility made her heart sink.
"We have to get back to the temple, now!" she exclaimed, running towards Bluey, but Qingyi stopped her at the last moment.
"What are you-" Her words were interrupted by a high-pitched squeal as Qingyi picked her up.
Without hesitation, he activated the Lightning Steps.
Bluey was a majestic and fast animal, but she was nowhere near the speed of a Foundation Realm cultivator with a movement technique.
Yueli clung to Qingyi’s cloak, his touch not even registering in her agitated mind.
All she could think about was the danger her sisters were in.
Looking over his shoulder, she saw Bluey already galloping towards her.
She didn’t worry too much about the mare, she was an intelligent animal who knew the way home.
"Hold on tight!" Qingyi warned as his body surged over the treetops, his speed increasing even more.
Elize hummed softly as she removed the lid from a steaming pot.
She took a spoon and tasted the reddish broth that was boiling.
"Perfect!" She curled her lips as she went to put the lid back on, but stopped at the last moment, feeling the ground beneath her feet shake.
She ran to the other side of the kitchen, grabbed her sword and shot into the temple courtyard.
Her eyes fixed on the sky above the walls.
The temple’s defensive formations were active, a barrier of thunderous energy forming a dome around them.
That immediately made her heart sink.
The temple’s formations would only activate if there was a powerful enemy trying to invade the sect, and in its current state, it was too weakened.
They had no spirit crystals to power the formation, and the little energy that remained was only what the formation could gather from the environment.
"Big sister Elize! What’s going on?" The other priestesses approached, worried.
Their eyes soon focused on the sect’s large double gates when a crash echoed, the wood shuddering slightly.
"Go to the throne room and lock everything up. Yueli and Qingyi should be here soon," Elize ordered, putting all the strength she could muster into her voice as she drew her sword.
"But-"
"Now!" Elize interrupted the girls, forcing her aura out of her body and pushing them towards the throne room.
Although she was not yet at the Foundation Realm, she was the strongest of the priestesses who had stayed at the temple.
It was her responsibility to look after all the others.
The women obviously tried to stay and fight alongside her, but the purple-haired beauty wouldn’t give in.
They weren’t ready to fight without Yueli, Elize knew that well. It would be a bloodbath if she allowed them to take part.
With all her determination, she closed the large double doors of the throne room, locking them inside.
Unlike the formations surrounding the temple, the formations in the throne room were much more powerful and could hold Foundation Realm cultivators for many minutes.
If she herself could stop the enemies for a few more moments, it would certainly be enough time for Yueli and Qingyi to return.
"Ah..." she sighed, calming her breathing. She was terrified, but she didn’t let it show.
Her Lightning Qi took over the air around her and, with a powerful explosion, the double gates flew open, revealing rough-looking men with bald heads and red jackets.
’Red Claw...’ She gritted her teeth.
She’d expected them to come back at some point... but why now?
"Look what we’ve got here!" One of the bandits stepped forward, his eyes focusing on Elize’s body like a pig in heat.
Right behind him, she could see at least another hundred, but she relaxed the moment she realized that there were no Foundation Realm cultivators among them.
That made everything so much easier.
"The leader wouldn’t mind us having a bit of fun with her first, would he?" Another thug asked, causing Elize’s face to distort in anger.
Her shoulders shook as she stomped hard on the ground, catapulting herself towards him.
"Oh... she’s brave!" The bandit smiled disdainfully as he raised his sword, but the next moment, he regretted it.
Elize’s sword didn’t meet his.
On the contrary, it snaked around the blade like a bolt of lightning, finding his neck and hurling his head into the air.
Elize was not a fragile, delicate woman, at least not in front of any man other than Qingyi.
She had been trained by a sword master since she was six years old, and when she no longer had that master, she still had the temple library, with thousands of books on fencing and combat.
The bandits, on the other hand, had never faced anything but weak, unarmed peasants, the biggest battles of their lives being fought in brothels.
They were not on the same level.
"What the fuck?" The first bandit shouted, his eyes wide as Elize advanced towards him.
Her sword easily deflected his. Two bloody fists fell to the ground before her blade found his chest.
"Come!" She roared, her blood burning as her sword danced around her body.
She would hold them back until her knees failed and her shoulders slumped. As long as her sisters were in danger, she would endure.

chapters.title: Chapter 76 - "I’m sorry, honey... I made you suffer..."
paragraphs: "You bitch!" one of the bandits roared as he swung his sword in Elize’s direction.
The purple-haired beauty defended herself gracefully, taking only one step back before counterattacking.
Her blade sliced through the bandit’s shoulder, destabilizing him before ripping through his belly.
At the same moment, another bandit appeared behind her, his sword opening a deep gash in the young woman’s delicate back.
"Ghn~~" Elize grunted painfully before kicking backwards, throwing her aggressor away and quickly retreating.
More than twenty corpses already lay under her feet, but the number of enemies didn’t seem to be decreasing one bit.
"Cough! Cough!" She brought her hands to her lips and looked at the trembling palm bathed in blood.
Her vision blurred and she stumbled, almost falling.
’What’s happening, have I been poisoned?’ she thought, feeling the burning cut on her back.
No... this couldn’t be happening.
"Just a little bit more," she roared, her aura exploding with more power than ever.
Whatever was in her blood boiled as she pushed all her lightning Qi out of her Dantian.
She wasn’t ready to die, not yet.
How could she accept dying without even presenting the child she would have with her beloved to her mother?
But although she didn’t want to die, she wasn’t willing to back down and leave her sisters behind either.
She refused to be a coward, she didn’t want to lose her sisters like she had lost her mother and her master.
With a heavy heart and panting breath, she felt her meridians tremble violently.
"She’s trying to make a forced breakthrough!"
"Stop her!"
The higher-ranking bandits roared, directing their swords, machetes and axes at Elize. If she advanced to the foundation realm now, they would be in serious trouble.
"Die!" Elize’s voice echoed like a bestial scream.
The ground beneath her feet cracked as she channeled all the energy from the breakthrough into her sword. The metal shook, but didn’t break.
The first bandit reached her, his weapon coming within centimeters of the beauty’s delicate neck before she defended herself.
Her blade found his torso and sliced through bone and muscle until it came out the other side.
Without wasting time, she advanced to the next one, a decapitated head falling to the ground while her sword cut through the air.
"Keep attacking, don’t let her finish her advance!" shouted a bandit who was a single step away from the foundation realm before having his throat torn out.
Slowly, the bodies under Elize’s feet increased.
From twenty to thirty, from thirty to forty and soon, more than fifty bloody corpses covered the ground.
Her body was marked by dozens of cuts, some deep enough to reach her bones.
She was in the worst pain she had ever felt in her life, but she didn’t cry or even wince.
"Shit! She’s almost finished advancing to the foundation realm!" The bandits tried to retreat, feeling the Qi around Elize change drastically.
Forced advances were dangerous, even when successful, they usually left deep wounds and an unstable base.
Even so, they couldn’t help but shrink back in fear in front of that woman.
Their leaders had lied, saying that they were all weak and fragile women!
"You dared to come here, so you’ll stay here for the rest of eternity!" Elize roared, her voice hoarse as she swung her sword in fury.
But then her momentum suddenly stopped.
A metallic clang echoed as her sword shattered and she was thrown more than ten meters.
"Ugh... blergh..." She fell to her knees, vomiting blood and raising her gaze to a shadowy figure.
He wasn’t one of the leaders of the Red Claw gang, but he was still a Foundation Realm cultivator.
Her breakthrough had been a success and she could already feel the Qi core in her Dantian, but she was too injured to fight another cultivator of the same level.
She tried to get up, but her body didn’t respond.
Even using her Qi, all she managed was to shudder slightly before collapsing onto what was left of her sword.
"Ah... you gave us a lot of trouble, huh? But the leader likes women like you. I’m sure you’ll give him many powerful heirs once we’ve sorted out this mess."
The shadowy figure laughed, approaching her in quick steps, his eyes sweeping over the woman’s body lustfully.
Even with all her wounds, she was still an incomparable beauty.
"Husband... where are you?" She closed her eyes as his hands approached.
She prepared to bite her tongue and commit suicide, but stopped the last moment, hearing a heartbreaking scream and feeling a splash of blood on her face.
"Elize!" Yueli’s worried voice reached her ears and she opened her eyes.
Yueli hugged her tightly as she watched the handsome, powerful figure standing in front of her, holding the dark figure’s neck.
With a single squeeze, the handsome young man’s fists met, and the dark figure’s head was crushed like a ripe tomato.
"Don’t anyone dare move a single step," he ordered, and no one did.
Not out of obedience, but because they couldn’t.
Their bodies were crushed by a powerful aura, their knees already buckling as their hearts seemed about to explode.
Not even their leader had such overwhelming murderous intent... no, their leader’s murderous intent was like a child’s tantrum at what they felt exuding from that young man’s body.
Qingyi ignored them, his heart sinking as he looked at Elize’s bloodied body.
His hands were shaking as he bought the most expensive recovery pill he could get from the system.
His lust points reached zero and continued to drop until they reached two thousand negative points, but he didn’t care.
[I’ll allow this purchase, but if you don’t recover the points you’ve spent within 24 hours, the punishment will be severe].
Ignoring the system’s threats, he knelt down in front of Elize.
"H-husband..." she whispered, her voice weak as she watched Qingyi.
Her eyes slowly closed.
"I’m sorry, honey... I made you suffer..." He put the pill to his own lips and kissed Elize, forcing the pill down her throat.
Yueli obviously didn’t mind it, placing her hands on Elize’s back and helping her to calm her turbulent energy.
The effect was immediate.
Elize’s complexion soon became pinker and the wounds covering her body quickly closed up.
This was a pill no inferior to what cultivators of the nine peaks basin used, leaving not even a single scar behind.
Qingyi stood up and took a step towards the invaders.
There were still almost a hundred and fifty of them, but these numbers didn’t even make him blink.
Drawing his sword, he used the second form of the Tempest Monarch’s sword art

Even using her Qi, all she managed was to shudder slightly before collapsing onto what was left of her sword.
"Ah... you gave us a lot of trouble, huh?
But the leader likes women like you.
I’m sure you’ll give him many powerful heirs once we’ve sorted out this mess."
The shadowy figure laughed, approaching her in quick steps, his eyes sweeping over the woman’s body lustfully.
Even with all her wounds, she was still an incomparable beauty.
"Husband... where are you?" She closed her eyes as his hands approached.
She prepared to bite her tongue and commit suicide, but stopped the last moment, hearing a heartbreaking scream and feeling a splash of blood on her face.
"Elize!" Yueli’s worried voice reached her ears and she opened her eyes.
Yueli hugged her tightly as she watched the handsome, powerful figure standing in front of her, holding the dark figure’s neck.
With a single squeeze, the handsome young man’s fists met, and the dark figure’s head was crushed like a ripe tomato.
"Don’t anyone dare move a single step," he ordered, and no one did.
Not out of obedience, but because they couldn’t.
Their bodies were crushed by a powerful aura, their knees already buckling as their hearts seemed about to explode.
Not even their leader had such overwhelming murderous intent... no, their leader’s murderous intent was like a child’s tantrum at what they felt exuding from that young man’s body.
Qingyi ignored them, his heart sinking as he looked at Elize’s bloodied body.
His hands were shaking as he bought the most expensive recovery pill he could get from the system.
His lust points reached zero and continued to drop until they reached two thousand negative points, but he didn’t care.
[I’ll allow this purchase, but if you don’t recover the points you’ve spent within 24 hours, the punishment will be severe].
Ignoring the system’s threats, he knelt down in front of Elize.
"H-husband..." she whispered, her voice weak as she watched Qingyi.
Her eyes slowly closed.
"I’m sorry, honey...
I made you suffer..." He put the pill to his own lips and kissed Elize, forcing the pill down her throat.
Yueli obviously didn’t mind it, placing her hands on Elize’s back and helping her to calm her turbulent energy.
The effect was immediate.
Elize’s complexion soon became pinker and the wounds covering her body quickly closed up.
This was a pill no inferior to what cultivators of the nine peaks basin used, leaving not even a single scar behind.
Qingyi stood up and took a step towards the invaders.
There were still almost a hundred and fifty of them, but these numbers didn’t even make him blink.
Drawing his sword, he used the second form of the Tempest Monarch’s sword art

chapters.title: Chapter 77 - "I’ll rip your shoulders from your body"
paragraphs: Qingyi’s sword tore through the air in a horizontal slash, its thunderous aura transforming into a blade-shaped arc of Qi that flew towards the thugs of the Red Claw gang, expanding rapidly.
That was the second form of the Tempest Monarch Sword Art. Unlike the first form, which was a focused thrust, the second was broader, designed to kill as many enemies as possible.
Desperate screams echoed among the ranks of criminals as Qingyi’s attack reached them, tearing through flesh and bone with ease.
A bloody mess spread across the temple courtyard. But he ignored all this, his eyes turning to Yueli and Elize.
The purple-haired beauty was already out of danger, her eyelids slowly opening.
"H-husband..." she called out as Qingyi approached, her eyes watering and her body trembling as she tried to get up.
"Circulate your energy and recover. I’ve still got some pigs to slaughter..." he forced the gentlest, most loving smile he could muster, trying to suppress all the anger boiling up inside him.
It was difficult, but he didn’t want any of his women to suffer from his murderous intent.
’I’m sorry...’ he thought as his eyes met Yueli’s.
None of this would have happened if he hadn’t simply tried to take her at that very moment.
In fact, they wouldn’t even have come close to that danger if he hadn’t insisted on going with her.
He was foolish, but he didn’t torture himself too much about it either, there was no way he could have guessed.
The world of cultivation was dangerous, and he would never even leave the Foundation Realm if all he did with his life was hide and be afraid to make any decisions.
"Ah..." he sighed heavily as he turned his back on the two beauties and walked towards the temple gate.
The only way to truly guarantee the safety of his women was to completely exterminate his enemies the first chance he got.
Leaving the temple, he looked towards the forest.
"What are you waiting for? Do you still have more worms to send to their deaths?" Qingyi stopped his steps and soon two figures emerged from the depths of the forest.
The first was Hei Langya, a short, overweight man who wore a cruel smile and was at the fourth stage of the Foundation Realm.
The second was Hei Yeming, a little taller than his brother and at the fifth stage of the Foundation Realm.
"You must be the bastard who killed our brother, right? Say your name, I’ll make those whores write it in blood on your pedestal while we have fun with them!" Hei Langya growled, drawing his sword.
A flaming, hateful aura swept over him.
Qingyi didn’t care about that insult, it was beneath him.
His eyes remained cold and his smile strangely friendly as he spoke: "I’ll rip your shoulders from your body and leave you to die, bleeding like a pig."
His voice was calm and gentle, but still brimming with murderous intent, enough to make even hideous criminals like the Hei brothers take steps backwards.
"You damn pretty face!" Yeming roared, gathering his courage and also drawing his sword.
Two powerful Foundation Realm auras fell on Qingyi.
He didn’t even blink under that power. His own Qi exploded from his body, forcing the Hei brothers to take another step back.
Inside, he was a little worried. They remained too calm, even though they had realized his full power.
Calming his breathing, he used the first form of the Tempest Monarch Sword Art, lunging towards them.
"Watch out!" The two brothers raised their swords at the same time, forming a barrier of flames.
Qingyi’s Qi took the form of a giant sword tip as it tore through the ground and hit the flaming barrier.
A bang echoed. The flame barrier held Qingyi’s attack for a single second before giving way in an explosion of smoke.
Taking advantage of the thick curtain, Qingyi activated his draconic eyes and Lightning Steps. His body tore towards Hei Yeming.
"Son of a bitch!" Yeming barely raised his sword in time, parrying Qingyi’s blow.
His feet sank into the ground up to his heels as he was pushed back dozens of meters.
Qingyi was about to continue his attack when his senses screamed in alarm.
Hei Langya appeared beside him, his sword surrounded by scorching Qi, slashing towards his back.
The handsome young man turned his body. The scorching blade passed inches from him, cutting only a few strands of hair before hitting the ground.
"I said..." Qingyi gritted his teeth, his Qi reserves shuddering as he once again used the first form of the Tempest Monarch Sword Art.
"Ugh!..." Langya grunted as he tried to defend himself.
His arms went numb and his body was launched like a cannonball, bouncing off the ground several times until it hit a tree.
He coughed up large gulps of blood and reached into his pocket, pulling out a small spirit pill.
"You’ll regret being born, you bastard!" he roared as he brought the pill to his mouth, but it was too late.
Qingyi appeared above him, grabbing and crushing Langya’s fist. The pill fell to the ground along with bones and pieces of flesh.
"I said I’d rip your shoulders off, didn’t I?" Qingyi’s eyes were bloodshot as he grabbed Langya’s wrists and stomped on his chest.
He had no mercy.
His feet sank into the bandit’s ribcage as he pulled on his arms. The skin tore and the bones cracked as they were forcefully separated from the rest of the body.
"Argh... FUCK! STOP! STOP, MOTHERFUCKER! NOOOO!" Langya screamed desperately, but Qingyi ignored it.
For him, the pain Langya felt was only a fraction of what Elize had suffered.
A loud crack echoed as his collarbone finally broke, his shoulders being disconnected from his torso, an explosion of blood taking over where they used to be.
Langya’s screams echoed throughout the temple.
Yueli, who was still looking after Elize and had no view of the battle, couldn’t help but shudder at those horrendous sounds.
Was Qingyi really that furious?
